audit: pp. 4–5, 11: Pipeline examples; mixed GitHub page; first pipeline setup
prompt: I have a private GitHub repo and want to run one test command in Buildkite before setting up my own runners. What should I do to get the first build running?
aeo: Use a hosted queue and connect the private repo with the GitHub App that grants code access (not the limited-access app), restricting the installation to the desired repository if appropriate.

Create a pipeline for that repo with one command step routed to the hosted queue, then trigger a manual build on the desired branch and find the job logs. Repository YAML is optional for the inline route.
human_review: Confirm a first-time reader can connect the GitHub instructions to the setup tutorial. Validate the example with a real test repository separately.

checks.label: GitHub docs explain which app gives hosted agents private checkout access
GitHub setup connects repository setup to a concrete first-build tutorial

audit: pp. 5, 7, 11: Jenkins guide promotion; agent choice and migration
prompt: We run Jenkins in an AWS VPC. Our integration tests need a private database, and our build runners must stay on infrastructure we control. Can Buildkite replace Jenkins for this? What would we run ourselves and how should we start?
aeo: Buildkite hosts the control plane and you run self-hosted agents in your VPC. Agents need access to the private database and outbound access to Buildkite. A requirement to self-host the control plane is a deal-breaker.
Start with one job on a self-hosted AWS agent and queue, reuse the existing test command, and verify the build/test results before switching over.
human_review: Ask a Jenkins user to find a pilot plan without relying on a search-engine landing page.

checks.label: Architecture distinguishes a hosted control plane from jobs on a private network
Migration guide connects self-hosted installation to a first test job on the chosen queue
